Hibsago (bepirovirsen), the first antisense oligonucleotide for chronic hepatitis B virus.
Roche HBsAg II quant II RxDx was also approved as a companion diagnostic device to determine patients most likely to benefit from Hibsago.

The treatment was approved based on the results of two placebo-controlled trials. Results showed that 24% of patients who received Hibsago were able to stop their existing medication vs. none on placebo. Also, 24 weeks after ceasing all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago had HBV under control, with a protein that indicates infection not found in the blood.

Patients on Hibsago receive an injection up to every 24 weeks and continue to take other antiviral medicines. The approval is for adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV, and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less.
Labeling includes a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts.

title: GSK wins approval of bepirovirsen for hepatitis B
